subject: Atlas Health — post-call integration fit & SDK checklist
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Apr 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Atlas Health — post-call integration fit & SDK checklist

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap of what we heard and suggested next steps so your team has a single reference. Please flag anything I missed.

Top priorities you stated
- Real-time triage summaries for inbound patient messages (latency target: <250ms per chunk for streaming)
- Deterministic reranking of retrieved passages (preserve auditability and stable scores)
- On-prem data residency for PHI-sensitive logs (initially a VPC deployment, possible air-gapped later)

Constraints we discussed
- Minimal SDK changes on your side — prefer a light shim for function-calls vs. deep model plumbing
- Need structured outputs for downstream billing and CDS integration (JSON schema required)
- SOC 2 evidence + audit log export format (CSV/NDJSON)

Proposed integration approach (high level)
1) SDK: Add a small client-side adapter (Java/Node) that wraps Redwood streaming + function-calling — we can supply a 2-file shim and tests.
2) Streaming: Use chunked streaming for transcript windows; server-side KV caching for session affinity.
3) Rerank: Embeddings + hybrid reranker model; we will recommend quantized model variant for latency/cost.
4) Structured outputs: Enforce JSON schema via function-calling with Redwood's structured field validation.

Attachments: Integration checklist + short demo clip attached. I also attached a SOC 2 extract we referenced.

Next steps
- I’ll drop a draft integration checklist (attached) and a development timeline.
- Jonas will follow with a sample adapter repo and test harness by Tue 4/14.
- If procurement needs a ballpark, David, can you share your PO timeline?

If that all looks good I’ll get the follow-up doc out today.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
[evelyn.hart@redwood.ai]

--

From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@atlashealth.com>

Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@atlashealth.com>, David Li <david.li@atlashealth.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Apr 2026 18:11:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Atlas Health — post-call integration fit & SDK checklist

Evelyn —

Thanks for the clear recap. This matches our notes. A few clarifications and additions:

Clarifications
- Latency target: 250ms is ideal for the streaming chunks, but our absolute SLA to users can be up to 500ms for aggregated responses. Can we target 250ms P95 and 500ms P99?
- Rerank explainability: We need a way to export score deltas per candidate for audits. Can the reranker emit per-candidate metadata?

Must-haves
- JSON schema for structured output must include field-level provenance (model confidence + origin id).
- Retention controls: we need a 90-day configurable retention window before logs are exported to our archive.

Procurement note
- David: we need an initial ballpark for a 12-month reserved capacity (est. 2M tokens/day) and a demo environment NDA before we share any sample PHI.

Next steps from our side
- Priya will scope the engineering work and provide a 1-week estimate.
- We can run a small POC with synthetic data; procurement will come in once we have the ballpark.

Appreciate the attachments — I’ll confirm after reviewing.

—Samir
Director of Clinical Integrations
Atlas Health

Samir, Evelyn —

Thanks for the responses. Quick technical notes from the SDK/runtime perspective:

1) Adapter approach: We’ll provide a Node + Java adapter that exposes a single function-call surface for structured output. That adapter will translate your internal event model to Redwood function-calling payloads. Minimal changes to your existing services.

2) Streaming implementation: We propose using our chunked stream with per-chunk sequence IDs so your client can reassemble messages deterministically; this also allows partial early returns to UI.

3) Rerank metadata: The reranker can return per-candidate score and a short provenance token (source_doc_id, retrieval_method). We’ll include an option to export the per-request score table as NDJSON for audits.

4) Deployment: For the VPC plan we’ll surface a configuration toggle for retention window (30/60/90 days) and an automated export routine.

I attached a sample adapter README and a trimmed test manifest in the integration checklist. I’ll open a repo and post the link by EOD Tue (14th).

Jonas
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
